text:
maria (support): Heads-up: Acme escalated — after we renamed tool from `summary_v1` -> `text-summary`, their client calls to `summary_v1` are returning 404s. They claim this started after yesterday's rename rollout. Repro steps + logs below.

alex (eng-runtime): ack. do we have the exact client payload & sdk version?

maria (support): SDK 1.3.2 (python), sample curl they ran:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call_tool -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"tool":"summary_v1","args": {"text":"hello"}}'
```
Response: 404 {"error":"tool_not_found","tool":"summary_v1"} and registry log shows lookup miss.

jordan (eng-platform): hmm, rename propagation should create an alias entry. Did the registry migration create an explicit alias or only swapped canonical name?

alex (eng-runtime): checking. our migration did a name swap for canonical but for a short window we create an alias record. if the client's call hits an older cache layer (tool-gateway cache TTL 300s) they may see stale state. but 404s after 24h is suspicious.

sam (devex): customer says they still have SDK pinned to 1.3.2 (ship was yesterday). 1.3.2 has a known casefold quirk where it lowercases tool names before lookup. Could casing interplay with alias canonicalization?

lina (customer-success): Acme is in Private (VPC) deployment. They also said their platform has an internal caching proxy. Could be double-caching.

alex (eng-runtime): good point re: private deploy. The private registry sync job pushes changes from control plane -> private control plane; if that backfill failed, their private registry might be missing the alias. can we ask for a dump of their registry keys? (or I can run a check from our side if we have their cluster id).

maria (support): asked customer for `GET /registry/tools?name=summary_v1` response. They returned 404 from their control plane.

jordan (eng-platform): ok that confirms their private registry missed alias creation. likely a transient backfill error during the rename window. mitigation options: 1) re-run alias backfill for their cluster, 2) create a temporary redirect explicitly mapping `summary_v1` -> `text-summary`, 3) recommend client update to new tool name.

sam (devex): while we re-run backfill, can we provide a short-term patch on the SDK? a client-side shim that retries with casefolded name + canonical? Could help for a few customers.

alex (eng-runtime): avoid client-side hacks long-term. I'll queue an immediate backfill job for cluster id acme-487 and add a forced alias entry. Will post job id. Also adding a consistency check to alert if alias missing >5m after rollout.

devops-bot: backfill-job started: job-id fb-7721, targeting cluster acme-487. ETA 45s.

maria (support): forwarding job id to Acme. they asked for repro they can run to validate when complete. Suggest:```
# before: should get 404
curl -X POST https://private.acme.redwood/v1/call_tool -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"tool":"summary_v1","args":{"text":"x"}}'
# after: should return 200 and resolved to `text-summary`
```

devops-bot: backfill-job fb-7721 complete. created alias record summary_v1 -> text-summary.

alex (eng-runtime): verified alias present in private registry dump. Also noticed the alias's metadata `casefolded_name` was missing which explains break with SDK 1.3.2 lowercasing behavior. Patching to include casefolded_name.

jordan (eng-platform): follow-up actions: (a) add backfill retry metric to rollout checklist, (b) add alias `casefolded_name` during rename flow, (c) publish KB for private deploys about proxy caches + TTLs.

maria (support): Acme confirms calls now succeed. They ran the post-check and got 200. Thanks team. closing loop but please add postmortem notes and the KB link.

sam (devex): I'll draft a short KB and include the quick mitigation steps + repro. Will include the curl snippets and mention SDK versions with known casefold quirk.

alex (eng-runtime): quick note for the KB: if any SDK older than 1.4 lowercases tool names, the rename flow must write `casefolded_name` metadata; otherwise private registries + proxy caches can lead to persistent 404s.

lina (customer-success): filing customer follow-up: offer a small credit for their downtime and track as SEV-3.

maria (support): thanks everyone. marking thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
